title: Temporal Cohesion (Config Dumping Ground)
pattern: A single routine groups multiple operations together solely because they must execute around the same time (e.g., initialization, cleanup, or shutdown phases).
why_bad: Grouping unrelated actions (e.g., console banners vs. database TCP socket handshakes) makes it impossible to reuse, test, or modify them independently without triggering massive collateral dependencies.
detection: A function contains sequential calls to multiple disjoint subsystems or modules with no data flow or logical connection between them, other than execution order.
counterexample: A central main function or orchestrator that clearly sequences operations while keeping the actual implementation steps safely isolated in distinct modules.
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete, Chapter 7, Section "Aim for Strong Cohesion" (Temporal Cohesion)*
